safety_overall: The safety landscape is dominated by severe pressure integrity failures in both candidates. Candidate 1 operates at 15 bar, which is within the pump limit (20 bar) but leaves only 33% headroom, creating a significant risk of overpressure if flow resistance increases (e.g., due to particulate or temperature drop). Candidate 2 is physically impossible to run as specified, with a calculated pressure drop of 47.5 bar exceeding the pump's maximum rating of 20 bar by more than double; this is a hard BLOCK. Both candidates utilize FEP tubing, which is chemically compatible with acetonitrile at 21°C, but the mechanical stress from high pressure requires verification of the specific FEP rating (typically 10-15 bar for small ID, though high-pressure FEP exists, the system design is unsafe). The reaction involves singlet oxygen generation, requiring strict exclusion of air/moisture if sensitive, but primarily demands robust pressure containment. No thermal runaway risk exists (Da_thermal << 0.1).
